paper_metadata.title: Quantum and Classical Machine Learning in Decentralized Finance: Comparative Evidence from Multi-Asset Backtesting of Automated Market Makers

summary: The paper performs a 50‑experiment backtesting study (10 models × 5 runs) on 2024 crypto data (BTCUSDC, ETHUSDC, USDCUSDT). Classical models such as Random Forest achieve 13.16% return and Sharpe 1.68, while pure quantum models perform poorly (VQE 3.00% return, Sharpe 0.79; QNN 4.47%, Sharpe 0.82). Hybrid models perform best overall, with QASA Sequence reaching 13.99% return and Sharpe 1.76, but no practical quantum advantage over classical methods is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Pure quantum variational classifier (VQE Classifier) used as a backtesting model for AMM/DeFi rebalancing prediction on crypto assets.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are normalized to [0, 2π] and mapped to 6 qubits; the paper states 6-8 features for quantum models and a 6-qubit VQE classifier.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of whether rebalancing should occur, y_t ∈ {0,1}.

problem_instance.description: Crypto AMM/DeFi rebalancing prediction across BTCUSDC, ETHUSDC, and USDCUSDT using daily data over 2024.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Time-series split 70% train / 15% validation / 15% test; angle encoding for quantum features.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical features include price, volatility, volume, time, microstructure, lagged, and interaction features; quantum models use a compact 6-8 feature subset mapped to angles.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 5 independent runs per model; backtesting metrics and model metrics reported on the test split.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Angle encoding of normalized features; time-series split; feature engineering from market data.
